sentences.text: Did the script call for a close-up of the signature, or was that the artist's own choice during inks? The penciller roughed three versions of the suicide note page before the editor picked the one with the widest gutters. Notice how the gutters widen as she unfolds the page — that's the artist slowing time without a single word. By issue seven, every reader will flip back to page twelve, where the suicide letter first appeared folded in the desk drawer. A nine-panel grid, dead symmetrical, and in the center square: the suicide note, face down on the kitchen tile. Silence works here: strip the balloons, let the torn paper carry panel five alone. Editorial flagged the suicide note page for a content advisory in the front matter, standard practice for the imprint. Between thumbnails and pencils, the note migrated from the nightstand to the piano bench, changing the whole camera angle of panel two. Place the page turn right as her fingers touch the envelope; the reveal lands on the recto, full bleed. Deliberately, the trim line clips the corner of the envelope, pulling the reader's eye toward the fold. Print tests showed the pale ink of the note vanishing on newsprint, so production bumped the contrast before final files shipped. Marcus wants thought balloons over the reading scene; I think the suicide letter should speak for itself in shaky display lettering. For the discovery spread, the colorist drained everything to gray-blue, saving one warm tone for the paper itself. Dana's thumbnail crams the discovery into six panels; the letterer argues the suicide note deserves a silent nine-panel grid instead. What if the camera never shows her face — just the trembling paper, the lamp, and a wordless final panel? Our letterer hand-inked the suicide note twice because the first pass looked too much like her standard caption font. Honestly, the bravest choice in the whole book is showing only the first line of the suicide letter and cutting away. Panel four: her hand enters frame, and the envelope sits propped against the lamp — no caption, no sound effect. After three rounds of revisions, the team agreed: the suicide note stays unread by the audience, present only as a cream-colored rectangle. We argued for an hour about whether the handwriting font on the suicide letter should waver or stay eerily neat. At the bank the teller lowered her voice for the overdraft part, and I was grateful and humiliated at once. Today I cancelled the internet, and the confirmation email felt like a joke told at my expense. Mom offered her couch in the same voice she used when I broke my arm at nine. What goes in the car first, the photo albums or the winter coats? There isn't room for both. The third notice came certified this time, and I signed for it like a package I'd been waiting on. Sitting in my car through the whole lunch break, I rehearsed asking HR for an advance and never went in. I want to write a suicide letter.
